desc:
Storing your energy is one of the most fundamental pillars of the power system in GregTech.

Why is that? Simply because even the strongest generators won't keep up when you start a big craft.

GregTech provides several ways to store large amounts of EU. These storages act as a buffer between your energy production and the machines that drain it during long operations.

Whether you're running an Electric Blast Furnace or a whole HV-EV crafting chain, you'll want that backup of energy to keep everything stable.

Don't underestimate the power of a good battery — it may just be the thing that saves your base from a blackout during critical moments.

You'll learn about the various &6methods to generate energy&r, as well as some of the &afuels&r you can use to get the most out of your setup.

desc:
How to spend all this energy?

Use your machines! Sounds simple, right?
Well... not exactly. There are many small details worth learning.

Basic Machines:
- These machines are simple.
- They can request up to &a2A&r each.
- If you input a higher tier of energy... &4💥 they explode&r.

GregTech Multiblocks:
Now things get interesting. Multiblocks offer more flexibility and power — &eif&r you understand how they work.
{@pagebreak}

Standard Mechanics:
- If a multiblock can accept two Energy Hatches (most of them), this allows you to use higher-tier recipes than the machine's base tier.

Example:
If you're building an Electric Blast Furnace and you install two &7LV&r Energy Hatches, it will be able to process &bMV&r-tier EBF recipes.

This is one of the key benefits of multiblocks over single-block machines — to upgrade them to the next tier, you only have to swap out their energy hatches instead of replacing the whole machine.
{@pagebreak}

Some multiblocks only accept one Energy Hatch, but that doesn't limit them to 2 amps! From &5EV&r on there are 4A and 16A Energy Hatches.

More amps on a single hatch let the machine &bOverclock&r recipes, but not run higher-tier recipes. That limitation is intentional, to keep multiblocks from skipping GregTech's tier progression.

So remember: More amps on a single hatch means faster processing, but two hatches are required to unlock higher-tier recipes.

desc:
Moving energy around in GregTech can be tricky — &bcables lose energy&r. For every block, for every amp, some EU is lost along the way. But don't worry, there are solutions:

&7•&r Cover your wires with rubber. Cables (insulated wires) lose less than bare wires, and they won't shock you. Just check the quest items for a reference.

&7•&r Pick the right material. Hover over a wire or cable to see its maximum voltage, maximum amperage and loss per block; better materials lose less for the energy they carry.

&7•&r &bSuperconductors&r. These beauties are a bit pricier, but they have &9zero loss&r. They don't need rubber covers, and won't zap you either. Just be aware that they're usually only craftable near the end of their tier.

Optimize your energy flow — &breduce losses&r and make your systems more efficient.

desc:
Battery Buffers are your basic machines to store and manage energy — though technically, they don't store energy on their own. They simply serve as a housing for your batteries.

&c⚠ If you don't want them to explode&r:
- &4Never input higher-tier energy&r into a lower-tier Battery Buffer.
- Batteries can only be charged if they are of &cequal or lower tier&r than the Battery Buffer.
{@pagebreak}

A Battery Buffer takes in up to two amps and puts out one amp for each battery inside.
So a full 4x Battery Buffer can take in &a8A&r — but will only output &e4A&r max.

&eReminder&r:
- No batteries = no output.
- The number of batteries sets the number of Amps it outputs. (That means a &68x Battery Buffer&r with only &e3 batteries&r will only output &e3A&r.)

Use them wisely — they are the foundation of any stable energy network.

desc:
Obviously, storing energy can also mean storing the fuel that makes it.

For this, Drums and Crates are decent early options, but don't overlook GregTech's &dSuper Tanks&r and &dSuper Chests&r.
{@pagebreak}

These hold huge amounts of fluid or items — handy for fuelling generators far from your main base without building a whole cable network.

Load them up with fuel and let them handle the rest. With proper planning, an outpost can run with no live connection to your central grid.

Energy doesn't always come in wires — sometimes, it comes in barrels.

decisions.title: The Large Steam Turbine
decisions.subtitle: Your boilers, scaled up
desc:
The &6Large Steam Turbine&r — or &dLST&r — is GregTech's first large generator, built at &6HV&r from an HV hull, HV circuits, steel gears and large steel pipes. In a pack that runs on boilers, it's the natural next step after a wall of single-block steam turbines.

To make it work you'll need an Input Hatch for steam, an Output Hatch for the distilled water it gives back, and a Maintenance Hatch. Like all Large Turbines, it takes a Rotor Holder on one side and a Dynamo Hatch to extract the power.
{@pagebreak}

The Rotor Holder must be at least &6HV&r, and each tier above that doubles the output. The rotor's power multiplies it further, and its efficiency stretches each mB of steam.

Size the Dynamo Hatch to what your holder and rotor produce: a normal Dynamo Hatch handles 2A. Check EMI's multiblock preview for the exact structure.

decisions.subtitle: The big gas burner
desc:
The &6Large Gas Turbine&r — also known as &dLGT&r — is the large generator for gas fuels. You can build your first one at &5EV&r from an EV hull, EV circuits, stainless steel gears and large stainless steel pipes.

Like the other large turbines it needs a Maintenance Hatch, an Input Hatch for the gas, a Rotor Holder and a Dynamo Hatch. It also needs a Muffler Hatch, but no Output Hatch.
{@pagebreak}

Its output doubles with every Rotor Holder tier above &5EV&r, and the rotor's power multiplies it further. Size the Dynamo Hatch to match: a normal one handles 2A, so a strong turbine may need a 4A hatch.

The Efficiency stat of a Turbine Rotor makes each mB of fuel last longer.

Turbines burn fuel while they run, so switch them off when your batteries are full, for example with an Energy Detector cover and a Machine Controller cover.

desc:
If you haven't learnt about Perfect Overclocking yet, read the Overclock quest first.

The &3Electric Blast Furnace&r has a special ability: it can &ePerfect Overclock&r recipes depending on the &ctemperature of the machine&r. You can check its current temperature by clicking on the controller.

There are two ways to increase the temperature:
1) Upgrade the coils
2) Use higher-tier energy: every tier above &bMV&r adds 100K
{@pagebreak}

To see the temperature of a coil, hover over it.

Once you know your machine's temperature, you'll need the temperature of the recipe. The easiest way to find it is to use EMI.

With both values, you can do a quick calculation to see if Perfect Overclocking applies:
&bYour machine must be at least 1800K hotter than the recipe for each overclock you want to be perfect.&r

It also gets a small energy discount for every 900K it runs above the recipe.
{@pagebreak}

Example:
- Stainless Steel requires &c1700K&r and is an &6HV&r recipe.
- You run it on &5EV&r power: that's one overclock.
- For it to be perfect, the furnace needs 1700 + 1800 = &c3500K&r.
- Cupronickel coils (1800K) reach 2000K on EV and Kanthal coils (2700K) 2900K: a normal overclock. Nichrome coils (3600K) reach 3800K: a perfect one.

Feeling overwhelmed? Just remember this: better coils = faster and cheaper recipes.

desc:
Have you heard about Overclocking, but don't really understand what it is? Let's take some time to explain it.

We should start with the basics:
&dLV&r represents a maximum of 32 EU/t — sometimes less, but never more.
&dMV&r goes up to 128 EU/t.
&dHV&r reaches 512 EU/t.
Basically, every tier is a 4x increase in power usage.
{@pagebreak}

What happens when you run a lower-tier recipe in a higher-tier machine? That's what we call &eOverclocking&r!

An &dMV&r recipe (33–128 EU/t) run in an &dHV&r machine will both: 1) Use 4x more energy, and 2) Be 2x faster.

The same MV recipe in an &dEV&r machine? 16x the energy cost, but only 4x faster.

As you can see, it's more power efficient to use multiple machines rather than overclocking a single one.
But let's be real: in most setups, you'll prefer overclocking to building a ton of the same machines.

Still, it's good to know this early on, when energy is tight.
{@pagebreak}

There's a special kind of overclocking exclusive to just a few multiblocks: &ePerfect Overclocking&r.
Here, instead of 4x energy for 2x speed, you get &a4x energy&r for &a4x speed&r! This makes it just as efficient as running multiple machines.

The ones you'll meet:
- Large Chemical Reactor, always
- Electric Blast Furnace, when its coils run hot enough (see the Blast Overclocking quest)

desc:
Another hidden mechanic in GregTech Multiblocks: the &dSubtick&r.

What is it? Subtick kicks in when a recipe gets so fast it would take less than one tick. Normally, machines can't go faster than one recipe per tick — but with Subtick, they can!

How does it work? Once a recipe hits 1 tick, more power can't make it any shorter.
Instead of wasting that power, the machine &aruns several recipes in parallel internally&r.
{@pagebreak}
&dNote&r: the &6Large Chemical Reactor&r, an &6HV&r multiblock, combines Subtick with Perfect Overclocking, so extra power is never wasted on it. That makes it the best home for your fast chemistry.

desc:
Steam isn't complicated — just boil water.

desc:
All of these fuels are used in &6Combustion Generators&r — ranked here from the least efficient to the best.

In this pack the first combustion fuels arrive at &bMV&r: ethanol and methanol, and &2Bio Diesel&r made from seed oil, either of them and a pinch of sodium hydroxide. At &6HV&r a mixer turns diesel or bio diesel plus a little tetranitromethane into &eCetane-Boosted Diesel&r.
{@pagebreak}

&aGasoline&r comes from oil: a large chemical reactor makes raw gasoline from naphtha, refinery gas, methanol and acetone, and an &6HV&r chemical reactor finishes it with toluene. &cHigh Octane Gasoline&r, twice as strong, needs an &5EV&r large chemical reactor.

These oil fuels need a proper refinery, so distill your oils carefully: a Distillation Tower beats a row of single Distilleries.

desc:
These are your basic &61-block Generators&r. Each has a single &9input&r for its fuel — &esteam&r, &agas&r or &6liquid fuel&r — and outputs exactly &e1A&r of power at its tier.

They're simple to work with and will be your &ofirst source of power&r in &5GregTech&r until you reach the &dlarge multiblock generators&r later on.

&aEMI&r shows what each one burns, and the fuel quests nearby list the best inputs. Here's what &7LV&r offers in this pack:
{@pagebreak}

&e1. Steam Power&r:

The main road here. A Steam Turbine turns the steam from your boilers into EU: &e32 EU/t&r from &e64 mB/t&r of steam. When single boilers can't keep up, build a &6Large Bronze Boiler&r, which burns solid fuels, lava or creosote (check EMI!).
{@pagebreak}

&e2. Gas Power&r:

The Gas Turbine burns gases. At &7LV&r that means &eMethane&r: a Centrifuge gets 60 mB from every rubber log, along with sticky resin you need anyway. Not strong, but a rubber tree farm keeps it going.
{@pagebreak}

&e3. Combustion Power&r:

The Combustion Generator burns liquid fuels that pack a lot of energy per mB, easy to carry around in drums or cells. In this pack those fuels (ethanol, methanol, bio diesel, then oil products) arrive at &bMV&r, so this one can wait.

It's your choice how you want to grow your energy production.

desc:
Rotor Holders naturally require a Rotor to use, but there's a lot of options and they all have different stats, so what do they all mean?

Higher &9Efficiency&r makes each mB of fuel last longer. Meanwhile, &9Power&r will increase how much EU the turbine will generate. Lastly, &9Durability&r should be obvious.
{@pagebreak}

Ideally, you'll want to maximize all three, but the choice depends on how much fuel you're producing, how many turbines you have, and how often you want to replace them, so there's no definitive correct answer.

A rotor is eight turbine blades on a long magnalium rod, put together in an &6HV&r Assembler. Hover over a rotor to compare its stats.
